Omar (VoltMedia): Heads up — our synthetic checks flagged a p99 regression starting around 2026-01-08T11:05Z. p95 up from ~210ms to ~760ms, p99 ~1.8s. We only serve redwood-llama-70b in ap-northeast-1 and noticed this after the quant rollout. Any chance this is related to a quant profile change?

Lena (Support): Sorry you're hitting this, Omar. I'll escalate and get eng to triage. Can you confirm the profile and whether you saw any error 5xxs?

Omar (VoltMedia): Profile header we set is X-Quant-Profile: int8_aggressive_v2. No code changes on our side. A few 503s during the spike. Quality change is subtle but main issue is tail.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-01-08T10:58Z completed (release/quant-opt-v2). Canary 10% -> 100% at 10:58:40Z :rocket:

Priya (eng-ml): jumping in. Looking at traces for ap-northeast-1 around 11:05Z. I'm seeing two likely causes: 1) per-shard calibration is happening at first request with this profile and takes ~350-600ms depending on layer mix, 2) some runs hit a dtype-range check that triggers a fallback to fp16 on a subset of layers and that fallback path currently does extra memcopy which adds jitter.

Julian (eng-runtime): confirming logs show "quant_profile=int8_aggressive_v2 calib_start" and "quant_range_overflow fallback_fp16 layer=23". Also found a sporadic log: "calib_cache_mismatch seed=0x7f -> expected=0x5a" which suggests calibration caches (when present) are not being validated correctly and cause re-calibration. I'll paste redacted snippets.

Priya (eng-ml): sample log from worker ap-1-wk-12 (sanitized):

```
[2026-01-08T11:05:12Z] shard=2 worker=ap-1-wk-12 event=calib_start profile=int8_aggressive_v2
[2026-01-08T11:05:12Z] shard=2 event=calib_layer idx=1 dur=24ms
[2026-01-08T11:05:12Z] ...
[2026-01-08T11:05:12Z] shard=2 event=calib_layer idx=44 dur=412ms
[2026-01-08T11:05:12Z] shard=2 event=calib_done total=518ms
[2026-01-08T11:05:13Z] shard=2 event=infer req=nm-20260108 lat=820ms
[2026-01-08T11:05:13Z] shard=2 event=quant_range_overflow layer=23 action=fallback_fp16
[2026-01-08T11:05:13Z] shard=2 event=calib_cache_mismatch seed=0x7f expected=0x5a
```

Julian (eng-runtime): that cache_mismatch is concerning. We have a new calibration cache v2 format in this release and some workers are still trying to read older v1-style caches which causes them to ignore the cache and recalibrate. That explains repeated calibrations and tail spikes when pools scale.

Sam (oncall): immediate mitigations for VoltMedia:
- flip their account/profile to fp16 so they bypass all quant paths
- temporarily set header override X-Quant-Profile: fp16 on their requests (support can do this per-account)
- bump ap-northeast-1 pool min_replicas to 2 to avoid repeated cold calibration
- if urgent, roll back quant-opt-v2 in ap-northeast-1 only
Which would you prefer?

Omar (VoltMedia): please set fp16 for now and bump min replicas. We need stable latency for the next 12 hours while you investigate.

Lena (Support): Applying fp16 override for VoltMedia now and asking infra to bump min_replicas. I'll post results in ~3m.

infra-bot: scaling policy updated: ap-northeast-1 pool min_replicas bumped to 2 for account VoltMedia (applied by infra-ops)

Lena (Support): FP16 override applied. Omar, any change in your metrics?

Omar (VoltMedia): quick look: p95 back to ~220ms and p99 ~530ms. 503s stopped. Thanks. We'll keep on fp16 while you fix this.

Priya (eng-ml): proposed engineering fixes and follow-ups:
1) fix calib-cache format handling: accept both v1 and v2 at runtime and add strict validation of seed/hash to avoid silent misses
2) precompute calibration caches during CI build/deploy and upload to S3 per model+profile so workers can pull a ready cache at startup (reduces first-request costs)
3) background calibration switch: return fp16 for the first request and swap to int8 only after successful cached calibration, avoiding blocking latency for first-hit
4) add a "predictable" quant profile that disables fp8 mixing and aggressive per-layer re-quant for customers with tight tail SLOs
5) telemetry: add metrics quant.calib_total_ms, quant.cache_hit, quant.fallback_fp16_count and attach to traces so Support can quickly correlate tail events

Julian (eng-runtime): I'll implement compatibility layer for calib-cache formats and add a debug flag to force cache acceptance for staging rollout. Also will remove the extra memcopy on the fp16 fallback fast-path to reduce jitter.

Priya (eng-ml): short repro steps for QA/staging (do not run on prod):
1) run runtime with new release but empty cache dir: `--model redwood-llama-70b --quant-profile int8_aggressive_v2 --calib-cache-dir=""`
2) set autoscaler to aggressive scale-down: min_replicas=0 scale_down_delay=2m
3) kickoff warmup that hits every shard to force calibrations:

```
for i in 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7; do
  curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/generate \\
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
    -H "X-Model-Profile: int8_aggressive_v2" \\
    -d '{"prompt":"warmup for shard '"$i"'","max_tokens":64}' &
  sleep 0.25
done
```

4) watch logs for calib_start/calib_done and quant_range_overflow/fallback_fp16 to see tail vs warmed latencies.

Julian (eng-runtime): test tip: to reproduce the cache_mismatch easily, start with a v1 cache file in the cache dir and use `RUNTIME_CALIB_DEBUG=1` env to log seed mismatches.

Sam (oncall): action items and owners:
- Lena: confirm ticket updated and customer notified of fp16 change + weekly updates until fixed owner: Lena ETA: immediate
- Priya: implement precompute calib-cache + background calibration plan and add docs for profile differences owner: Priya ETA: 2 weeks for prototype
- Julian: implement calib-cache compatibility + remove fp16 fallback memcopy + add quant telemetry metrics owner: Julian ETA: 5 business days
- infra-ops: add autoscaler safeguards for quant rollouts and per-region rollback playbook owner: infra-ops ETA: 3 business days

Omar (VoltMedia): good summary. Please include a short note on quality differences between fp16/int8/fp8 for our engineers. We'll coordinate a verification run when caching is ready.

Priya (eng-ml): will add a short customer-facing note: fp16 = stable and predictable; int8_aggressive_v2 = potentially lower steady-state latency but can incur first-request calibration costs and rare fp16 fallbacks that spike tail; int8_predictable (planned) = middle ground. We'll include eval diffs for customers to review.

Lena (Support): closing the escalation for now since VoltMedia is stable on fp16. Reopen if anything changes or if they want to trial cached int8 later. :white_check_mark:
